Timothy Morris for swooping in at 
the last moment like a superhero, Dr. Neill Matheson for his kind encouragement, and especially 
Dr. Timothy Richardson for his patience and insight, as well as for guiding me toward and 
through the wild world of rhetoric. 
Thanks are due to Dr. Kathryn Warren for being such a keen and supportive academic advisor 
and to Yael Sasley for being ever ready to help this hapless scholar navigate the electronic 
bureaucracy.

Philip attended John Eaton Elementary School from 1936 to 1938.10 
The Macomb Street residence is notable for its appearance in Dick’s later reflections; he 
recalled a "sunlit summer day" in Washington where the "ultrafantastic" began to bleed into his 
daily reality, a precursor to the porous boundaries of his fiction.13 During this time, Dorothy 
wrote pamphlets for the Federal Children’s Bureau, an environment that likely influenced Philip’s
